key_insight: The paper proposes that fully developed isotropic turbulence can be modeled as an SO(3) gauge theory with spontaneous symmetry breaking, separating the flow into a massless cascade sector and a massive, filament-confined vortex sector.
engineering_relevance: If valid, this framework could give fluid engineers a new physics-based way to predict when energy stays in the background cascade versus concentrates into intense vortex filaments.
method: Map angular momentum L = r × u to an SO(3) gauge connection and radial velocity u_r to a Higgs field.
Model the turbulent state with an SO(3) Georgi-Glashow theory that breaks to U(1) when radial strain condenses.
Compare theory to high-resolution DNS/JHTDB turbulence data using spectra, vortex-core profiles, and Wilson loops.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports DNS validation on JHTDB at Re_λ ≈ 433, including an inertial-range spectral split, BPS-like vortex-core fits, and an area-law Wilson loop with estimated string tension.
watch_item: The gauge-theory interpretation is highly nonstandard, so its physical meaning, parameter robustness, and generality beyond the reported dataset need careful independent verification.
paper_title: An SO(3) Gauge Theory of Turbulence with Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking
